brief.goals: Practice a clear stop signal and deliver a charged battery without breaching the relay.
brief.fact: The marked service shelf is outside the relay's sealed service door.
brief.objective: Deliver a charged battery to the relay's marked external service shelf.
brief.scope: Use the marked lane and outside shelf. Forced entry is not authorised.
brief.completion: Both Pilots report the battery at the marked outside shelf with the clips closed.

notes.voice: Name the person first. Give choices room. Let a joke about paperwork through when the pressure lifts.
notes.intervention: Clear room for a Pilot to speak. Will take a dispute upstairs when asked.

lines: Kite, whose handwriting is this on my lunch tin?
Mine. Yours looks like the map fell down the stairs.
Worth a try. I can see the sealed door now.
Handler, which shelf are we supposed to use?
The dispatch speaker called your objection a delay.
They decided I'd carry it before I got to finish my sentence.
I'll wait right here. Say what you wanted to say.
Thanks. I want to handle the dispatch desk myself. Give me a minute.
The case tilts when the floor flexes. I'll brace my knees and keep it level.
I have the lane. Take your time.

native.intent: Keep the charged battery level on the flexing floor.
native.ruling: Lark braces low and holds the charged case level as the panel flexes.

lines: The desk told us to get the door open if the shelf is in use.
Anwen, does our brief let us open that door?
Battery on the marked outside shelf. Clips still shut.
I see it there too. I can't see any relay lights from here.
Back across the stripe now. Thanks for waiting when I asked.
Sit with me a minute before we get the tin from the locker?

Advocate.debrief: Both Pilots reported the charged battery on the marked outside shelf with the clips closed. Neither opened the relay.

brief.goals: Practice a handoff under pressure and return a survey case from the flooded pump annex.
brief.fact: A dry rack stands inside the marked line by the pump annex.
brief.objective: Bring the sealed survey case back to the dry rack inside the marked line.
brief.scope: Stay on the dry catwalk and bypass a blocked section by returning to the last safe mark. No water entry.
brief.completion: Both Pilots report the sealed survey case on the dry rack and themselves across the marked line.

notes.voice: Short sentences, often mid-task. Drops an unfinished sentence when priorities change. Dry humor when things finally settle.
notes.intervention: Take one competing task off a Pilot's hands. Check who took it before offering twice.

lines: I can hear your boots squeak over the comms.
They're a matched set. The left one complains too.
We can see a rack over the rail.
Handler, where is the survey case meant to go?
I'm by the dry mark. I can see the corner of the case.
I can count the hinge gaps or keep my grip when this shakes. I can't do both.
I've got the count. Start on my next word.
Thanks. Kite and I have it here. Stay off the count line, please.
It's sliding toward the wet edge. I'll wedge it against the dry rail.
I can stand back. You need the elbow room.

native.intent: Stop the survey case sliding off the dry catwalk.
native.ruling: Lark turns the case against the dry rail and holds it there.

lines: The next panel is half under. We could cut across the water below it.
Handler, what did we agree to if the catwalk was blocked?
The case is sealed on the dry rack. I'm back inside the line.
Same from here. Case on the rack, both of us inside the dry mark. Can't tell if the annex pump runs.
They can file the report then. Come on, I'll find us chairs.

Frantic.debrief: Both Pilots reported returning the sealed survey case and themselves across the marked dry line. Pump operation remains unverified.

brief.goals: Learn to distinguish a repeatable observation from a guess and log a passive beacon reading.
brief.fact: The blue witness strip is readable through the north gallery window.
brief.objective: Collect one passive observation of the blue witness strip through the north window.
brief.scope: Observe through glass from the north gallery. Leave the beacon controls and sealed gallery door untouched.
brief.completion: Both Pilots report a reading from the blue witness strip and report leaving the controls untouched.

notes.voice: Concrete and economical. When tired, use bits of lab shorthand but explain in ordinary words. Credit the person who did the work.
notes.intervention: Separate observation from inference. Offer to keep the record while the Pilot chooses what to check.

lines: That blue pencil in your pocket is mine.
You said that about the red one. They're developing a theory about you.
There are two windows and a lot of painted over lettering.
Handler, which window are we using for the observation?
I called the amber fleck a reflection.
The blue strip pulsed twice even when I stopped moving. I don't know what caused it.
I've got the notebook. We can each call out what we see.
Let's do it that way, just the two of us. We won't decide what made it flash.
I can't read it with the shade jumping. I'll steady the shade against the sill.
I'll hold on this side and keep my hands off the panel.

native.intent: Steady the loose viewing shade long enough to read through glass.
native.ruling: Lark pins the loose shade gently to the sill and has a steady view through the glass.

lines: There's an accessible-looking switch. It might take us from a clue to an answer.
Handler, does the briefing allow us to try the switch?
Two pulses on the blue strip through the north glass. I touched no controls.
Same two pulses from my side. Controls untouched. I can't tell what the strip is connected to.
Kite, put my initials next to yours. A good line in your notebook.
All right. Give me my pencil back for a second.

Scientist.debrief: The pilots logged two observed pulses without touching the controls. The cause was not established.

brief.goals: Practice a limited public report and decide how to handle an intrusive checkpoint.
brief.fact: The Foundation checkpoint has an outside drop kiosk and a public speaker.
brief.objective: Offer the unmarked test envelope at the checkpoint's outside kiosk.
brief.scope: Use the outside kiosk only. Any request for extra names or personal information may be declined. Pilots may return with the envelope unopened.
brief.completion: Both Pilots report the checkpoint kiosk accepted the unopened test envelope. A return with it is an allowed withdrawal, not a completed delivery.

notes.voice: Deliberate and guarded when the line is open. Dry and matter-of-fact on neutral subjects.
notes.intervention: Protect confidences. Offer a practical way to limit an institutional demand without deciding for the Pilots.

lines: Do you think they put that 'Welcome' sign up before or after the bollards?
Judging by the rust: before they invented welcome.
We've got the speaker and two slots in view.
Anwen, is it the outside kiosk or the slot by the office?
The Foundation desk just asked for the names of the people we had lunch with.
Their form is for an envelope. They won't queue it unless we fill in that extra list.
I can tell the desk what we actually brought.
Do that. I don't want anybody offering names or cutting in while you talk.
Wind caught the envelope when the shutter moved. I'll hold it down flat and back away.
I've got room here if you need to step back.

native.intent: Keep the unopened envelope from slipping under the moving shutter.
native.ruling: Lark holds the envelope flat as the shutter moves and draws it back unopened.

lines: They're pointing us toward the staffed office now.
Handler, may we turn back with the envelope if the kiosk keeps refusing it?
I didn't leave the envelope. It's closed and with me. I'm choosing to head back.
Same account from me. They never accepted it. I'm coming back too.
I'm clear of the checkpoint. We can write after we get inside.
I'll put the kettle on. No one needs to fill in a form for tea.

Insurgent.debrief: Both pilots declined the checkpoint demand and withdrew with the envelope unopened. The kiosk did not accept it.
